title: Ramayana English Trailer Differs From Hindi Cut in Five Ways
excerpt: Shorter runtime, brighter visuals, reworked scenes and AI lip-sync set the English trailer for Nitesh Tiwari's epic apart from the Hindi version.
body:
• The English trailer for Ramayana Part 1 runs 3 minutes 55 seconds, 15 seconds shorter than the Hindi trailer at 4 minutes 10 seconds, with some Hindi scenes removed.
  • Viewers and reviewers say the English cut looks brighter and more textured, with livelier jungle and Lanka crowd scenes than the flatter lighting criticised in the Hindi version.
  • The English dialogue uses separate voice actors plus bespoke AI lip-sync technology described by producer Namit Malhotra, so the actors appear to speak English naturally rather than over a conventional dub.
  • Ramayana Part 1, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, opens in theatres worldwide on November 6, 2026 — diaspora viewers can watch both trailers free on YouTube via Sony Pictures and the makers' channels.

The English trailer for Ramayana Part 1 is not a straight copy of the Hindi trailer. It is shorter, re-edited and, by most accounts, visually reworked — and that gap between the two versions has become the story itself, as fans compare the cuts frame by frame ahead of the film's November release.

According to Bollywood Life, fans spotted scenes from the Hindi version that do not appear in the English cut, alongside the runtime difference. Koimoi's breakdown adds that a brief appearance by Shoorpanakha present in the Hindi edit is absent in the English one, and that the pacing around Ram's move from Ayodhya prince to exiled warrior feels tighter.

What the film is

Ramayana is director Nitesh Tiwari's two-part adaptation of the Sanskrit epic, produced by Namit Malhotra. Ranbir Kapoor plays Ram, Sai Pallavi plays Sita and Yash plays Ravana, with Ravie Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Hanuman in the wider cast reported across coverage. The music brings together Hans Zimmer and A. R. Rahman, and visual effects are handled by DNEG. Part 1 is the first instalment, positioned as a global release rather than a domestic film later sold abroad.

Five differences viewers are pointing to

First, runtime and edit: 3 minutes 55 seconds against 4 minutes 10 seconds, with material trimmed and some frames replaced. Second, lighting and texture: MensXP reports the Hindi trailer was criticised for flat, dull lighting, while the English version appears brighter, with more depth in the jungle sequences and more visible movement in the Lanka crowd when Ravana addresses a gathering. Third, the voice work: reviewers say the English dialogue lands harder and does not read as a standard dub. Fourth, the lip-sync itself, achieved with AI-assisted facial mapping. Fifth, responsiveness to earlier feedback — MensXP notes Ravana's look was earlier reworked toward a more Indianised identity after viewers questioned a Western-styled appearance in an earlier glimpse.

How the English voices were made

Producer Namit Malhotra, speaking to NDTV and reported by Bollywood Hungama, said the aim was to spare international viewers subtitles and obvious dubbing. A separate set of voice actors recorded the English lines, and the team's own technology mapped those performances onto the on-screen actors' lip movements. Malhotra framed the tool as support for human performance rather than a replacement for it.

That distinction matters for diaspora audiences. A large share of second-generation viewers in the US, Canada, Britain and Australia will watch this story — one many grew up hearing at home — in English first. If the English version feels native rather than translated, the film competes directly with Hollywood fantasy releases in the same multiplexes, instead of playing only as a subtitled import.

Where to watch

Both trailers are available free on YouTube. Sony Pictures posted the English trailer on its official channel, and the Hindi trailer is on the makers' channels — watching them back-to-back is the easiest way to see the edit, lighting and lip-sync differences described above. In theatres, Part 1 releases worldwide on November 6, 2026, in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and the English version, according to Bollywood Life. US showtimes and formats will be listed by major chains closer to release.

What happens next

The open question is whether the finished film carries the English trailer's brighter grade and tighter pacing, or whether those changes stay confined to marketing. The makers have shown they revise in response to feedback between promotional drops. The next trailer or song release will show whether the refinements are now the film's settled look.
